ai.description: The Bombay Night Frog is a medium-sized amphibian (35–45 mm) with a brownish-grey body and dark mottling. It features prominent, horizontally dilated pupils and distinct, fleshy, wrinkled skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus humayuni* is best distinguished by its distinctively elongated, pointed snout and the presence of prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips compared to other species.
ai.habitat: The Bombay Night Frog inhabits the humid evergreen forests and riparian zones of the Northern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 400 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bombay Night Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits unique "foot-flagging" behavior, where males extend their hind legs to signal to rivals and potential mates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus humayuni* breeds during the monsoon (June–September), laying clutches of 30–50 eggs on rocks or vegetation near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus humayuni* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 400 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Bombay Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "ticking" sounds, often heard near fast-flowing streams within the Western Ghats' dense forest canopy.
